title: Search for stable hadronising squarks and gluinos with the ATLAS experiment at the LHC
extended_summary:
This paper reports a particle physics search for long-lived massive particles produced in proton-proton collisions at the LHC, specifically coloured supersymmetric sparticles that may hadronize into stable R-hadrons. The central question is whether ATLAS can observe slow-moving, charged or intermittently neutral particles through detector signatures such as ionisation energy loss in the pixel detector and time-of-flight in the tile calorimeter.

The study uses 34 pb−1 of ATLAS data collected at a center-of-mass energy of 7 TeV. Candidate events are selected with missing transverse energy triggers and tracks consistent with a heavy, slowly moving particle; background is estimated with a data-driven approach. The analysis considers several interaction models for R-hadrons in matter and evaluates stop, sbottom, and gluino hypotheses.

No significant excess over Standard Model expectations is found. The paper sets 95% confidence-level lower mass limits of 294 GeV for sbottoms, 309 GeV for stops, and 562–586 GeV for gluinos depending on the interaction model, concluding that these are the most stringent limits available at the time.
quality_tier_rationale: This paper is a high-energy physics search from the ATLAS experiment, not an education study. It contains no intervention, learner, or instructional methodology relevant to ChatGPT, generative AI, or middle school mathematics achievement.
impact_tier_rationale: There is no educational outcome or instructional impact reported. The paper provides no evidence about student achievement, technology-supported learning, or school practice.
